family.description: This domain can be found in a group of proteins, including archaeal 6-hydroxymethylpterin diphosphokinase (6-HMDPK), known as MptE, which catalyses the formation of 6-hydroxymethyl-7,8-dihydropterin diphosphate (6-HMDP) from 6-HMD and ATP [[cite:PUB00061602]]. 6-HMDP is the precursor of the pterin containing moiety of the essential C1-carriers tetrahydrofolate and tetrahydromethanopterin. This entry also includes a number of uncharacterised proteins from bacteria.
family.name: 6-hydroxymethylpterin diphosphokinase MptE-like

causal_graphs.context: 3.5 ng enzyme with 100 uM 6-HMD and 1 mM ATP in 200 uL containing 8 mM MgCl2, 16 mM DTT and 40 mM TES/KCl pH 7.4; argon, 70 C, 10 minutes. Products detected after iodine oxidation.

evidence.explanation: Results, original Figure 4D and Methods 3.8-3.9; oxidized product matched a standard and desalted LC-ESI-MS/MRM. The figure displays PF0930, not a separate MJ1634 trace.

edges.mechanism: Purified PF0930 converts the supplied pterin in the joint reaction mixture to the diphosphorylated product. Zero-time, no-enzyme and matched nonexpressing-extract MonoQ controls support enzyme attribution; the source node does not make any single reagent sufficient.
edges.subject: enzyme_substrate_mix

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Q8U2A9 sequence 1/entry 94 is the 231-residue PF0930 reference; current InterPro PF01973 match is 37-183 inclusive. The study cloned PF0930 into modified pET24d; exact extra construct residues remain unverified. See evidence/PF01973/member-mapping.txt.
causal_graphs.limitations: Product identity is supported by chromatography, optical spectra and desalted MS, but no atomic mechanism, native flux or isolated Pfam truncation is tested. CTP/UTP/GTP retain activity, so ATP is not an exclusive donor. The monophosphate peak's origin is unresolved.

nodes.label: PF0930 reaction with 6-HMD, ATP and Mg2+

causal_graphs.scope: Recombinant P. furiosus PF0930/MptE, mapped to Q8U2A9; whole-protein biochemical activity, not isolated-domain sufficiency.
causal_graphs.title: PF0930 produces pterin diphosphate in a purified-protein assay

causal_graphs.context: Methods specify MJ1634 as an alternative enzyme in the same 70 C, 10-minute 6-HMD/ATP/Mg2+ assay used for PF0930. MJ1634 was expressed using pT7-7 in E. coli BL21-Codon Plus (DE3)-RIL and purified by heat treatment and MonoQ.

evidence.explanation: Figure 4D caption and Methods 3.4-3.5/3.8; supplementary Figure 4 independently documents the MJ1634 preparation, not its reaction time course.
evidence.snippet: Similar results were obtained with the MJ1634 protein.

edges.mechanism: The Figure 4D caption explicitly extends the biochemical result to MJ1634 and Methods specify its assay. The edge retains that report without transferring PF0930's displayed conversion percentage or claiming resolved catalytic residues.
edges.subject: enzyme_substrate_mix

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Q59028 sequence 1/entry 111 is the 241-residue MJ1634 reference, current PF01973 interval 32-196. The paper identifies NP_248644.1 and sequenced genomic clones; no isolated profile fragment was tested. See evidence/PF01973/member-mapping.txt.
causal_graphs.limitations: This is a reported whole-protein biochemical result, not independent inspection of a MJ1634 trace, raw kinetics or its own MS series. The original supplementary gel identifies MJ1634 fractions and notes CAT contamination in other lanes. Results and Methods differ on heat-treatment temperature.

nodes.label: MJ1634 reaction with 6-HMD, ATP and Mg2+

causal_graphs.scope: Recombinant M. jannaschii MJ1634/MptE, mapped to Q59028; the study reports similar biochemical results to PF0930 without a separate displayed MJ1634 chromatogram.
causal_graphs.title: MJ1634 has reported pterin diphosphokinase activity

causal_graphs.context: pBAD24-derived MJ1634 plasmid; LB with appropriate antibiotics, with or without thymidine, incubated 48 hours. Rescue is observed without arabinose induction. Empty vector, E. coli folK and thymidine supplementation are controls.

evidence.explanation: Genetic-validation Results, original Figure 4B and complementation Methods; Figure 4A concerns the different MJ0408/FolB system and is not this edge.

edges.mechanism: The archaeal clone restores growth under conditions in which the empty-vector folK deletion strain is thymidine dependent. Normal host partners remain present; the protein alone is not asserted to synthesize the entire cofactor.
edges.subject: mj1634_expression

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The sequenced genomic MJ1634 clone corresponds to Q59028/NP_248644.1; reference protein is 241 residues with PF01973 at 32-196. The experimental host differs from the archaeal reference taxon.
causal_graphs.limitations: Growth rescue is an indirect cellular readout. It does not measure native archaeal flux, cofactor concentrations, expression-normalized enzyme efficiency or the sufficiency of the isolated profile interval.

nodes.label: MJ1634 expression in the folK-deficient host
Growth on LB without added thymidine

causal_graphs.scope: M. jannaschii MJ1634 expressed in E. coli C600 delta-folK::tetB; heterologous complementation, not a native archaeal deletion phenotype.
causal_graphs.title: MJ1634 restores growth of an E. coli folK deletion strain

causal_graphs.context: PCR-checked short-linker gene replacement intended to minimize polar effects; AMB-1 grown/manipulated in MG medium at 30 C under microaerophilic conditions. Wild type and in-trans complementation provide comparisons.

evidence.explanation: Results and original Figure 1G-H plus Figure S4 compare wild type and deletion, including the modified and unmodified peptide spectra. No specific donor stereoisomer is asserted.

edges.mechanism: The deletion loses the approximately 70-kDa modified Fla band and detected nonulosonic-acid peptide modifications while approximately 55-kDa intracellular Fla remains. The mutation therefore affects maturation rather than simply abolishing all flagellin production.
edges.subject: maf_deletion

evidence.explanation: Results on HAL PDF page 9 and original Figure S1A-B on page 36; retained intracellular Fla is the important comparison, not evidence of a measured transport mechanism.

edges.mechanism: Anti-Fla probing of concentrated culture supernatants detects a wild-type signal but none in the deletion preparation. The edge describes detection in that assay, without resolving export versus extracellular stability or other intermediate causes.
edges.subject: maf_deletion

evidence.explanation: Original Figure 1D-E gives the deletion comparison; Figure 1F and Results provide rescue supporting attribution to maf. The edge does not join glycosylation and assembly into an observed molecular chain.

edges.mechanism: Electron micrographs show a filament in wild type and its absence in the maf deletion comparison. This is a downstream cellular phenotype; no direct assembly reaction is assigned to Maf.
edges.subject: maf_deletion

evidence.explanation: HAL PDF Results pages 8-9 explicitly describe deletion and rescue motility; Figure 1 shows associated filament phenotypes, not a direct motility measurement.

edges.mechanism: The authors report nonmotile deletion cells and recovery after maf complementation. This qualitative observation is not a quantified motility rate or proof that every Maf homolog controls motility.
edges.subject: maf_deletion

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Q2W9I6 sequence 1/entry 87, 666 residues, WP_011383128.1; PF01973 at 259-419, with separate PF20157/PF20156 domains. The paper's central structural region is 273-530. See evidence/PF01973/member-mapping.txt.
causal_graphs.limitations: Whole-protein deletion does not isolate catalytic-domain sufficiency. Loss of detectable extracellular Fla is not a measured export rate; filament and motility outcomes are not proof of a direct molecular link. The glycan remains pseudaminic acid or a close derivative, not stereochemically resolved.
causal_graphs.scope: Whole amb0685/maf deletion in Magnetospirillum magneticum AMB-1, currently Paramagnetospirillum magneticum; not a selective PF01973 deletion.
causal_graphs.title: Maf deletion disrupts flagellin maturation and motility in AMB-1

causal_graphs.context: Wild-type maf cloned into replicative pAK22 and introduced by conjugation; MG medium at 30 C and microaerophilic conditions. Comparisons are parental AMB-1 and its maf deletion.

evidence.explanation: Results and original Figure 1G-I, especially the complemented protein extract in panel I; Methods describe the wild-type complementation construct.

edges.mechanism: Supplying wild-type maf restores the approximately 70-kDa anti-Fla band lost in the deletion. The result supports gene-specific restoration of maturation, not direct observation of the glycosyl-transfer reaction.
edges.subject: wild_type_complement

evidence.explanation: Original Figure 1D-F compares parental, deletion and complemented cells by electron microscopy.

edges.mechanism: The complemented deletion strain again displays an external flagellar filament. This supports a downstream rescue phenotype without asserting direct assembly by Maf.
edges.subject: wild_type_complement

evidence.explanation: HAL PDF Results page 9 and complementation Methods pages 18-19; no supernatant-export rescue is added from Figure S1, which has only wild type and deletion.

edges.mechanism: The text reports recovery of cell motility following wild-type maf complementation. The causal effect is scoped to the tested deletion background and is not a separately quantified rate.
edges.subject: wild_type_complement

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Q2W9I6/WP_011383128.1 is the 666-residue Maf reference, with current PF01973 259-419 and terminal PF20157/PF20156 domains. Complementation is not restricted to the profile match.
causal_graphs.limitations: Rescue is conditional on other cellular factors and donor availability. No isolated-domain sufficiency, expression-normalized catalytic rate, supernatant-rescue assay or fully resolved glycan structure is established.

nodes.label: Wild-type maf supplied to the deletion strain

causal_graphs.scope: In-trans pAK22-maf complementation of the AMB-1 amb0685 deletion; whole-protein rescue in its cellular background.
causal_graphs.title: Wild-type Maf restores the AMB-1 deletion phenotypes

causal_graphs.context: Sequence-verified mutation plasmid; anti-Fla Western and reported optical-microscope motility readouts. The tested S283A, D318A and N491A constructs retain both readouts under the same study conditions.

evidence.explanation: Original Figure 5B and adjacent Results on HAL page 14 associate E324A with absence of the glycosylated-Fla band as well as the separately reported motility effect.

edges.mechanism: The E324A complement lacks the 70-kDa band obtained with wild-type maf and retained in the S283A/D318A/N491A comparisons. This records the band phenotype, not a measured intrinsic catalytic rate.
edges.subject: e324a_variant

evidence.explanation: Results accompanying Figure 5 explicitly describe the E324A complementation outcome; no quantitative motility measurement or rate is inferred.

edges.mechanism: Unlike wild-type maf, the E324A construct does not restore the reported motility phenotype. This is a downstream cellular effect, not evidence identifying the reaction's catalytic base.
edges.subject: e324a_variant

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Native Q2W9I6 residue 324 is E and lies within current PF01973 259-419 and the paper's structural 273-530 region. No isolated domain or E324A/D415A double mutant is implied.
causal_graphs.limitations: Loss of complementation can result from catalytic, folding, abundance or localization effects. The mutation experiment does not show matched Maf abundance/folding controls; anti-Fla is not an anti-Maf control. General-base chemistry remains hypothetical.
causal_graphs.scope: Single E324A substitution in full-length pAK22-maf expressed in the AMB-1 maf deletion strain; compared with wild-type complementation.
causal_graphs.title: E324A prevents Maf complementation of the tested readouts

causal_graphs.context: Sequence-verified mutation plasmid, anti-Fla Western and reported optical-microscope motility readouts; wild-type complementation and retained S283A/D318A/N491A responses provide comparisons.

evidence.explanation: Original Figure 5B, its Results and Table S2 identify the D415A single-mutant construct and its missing band; the shared sentence also describes E324A, not a double mutant.

edges.mechanism: D415A complementation lacks the 70-kDa anti-Fla band seen with wild-type maf and the study's tolerated substitutions. The experiment does not identify why D415A fails to support this maturation readout.
edges.subject: d415a_variant

evidence.explanation: Results accompanying Figure 5 name D415A among the noncomplementing constructs; Methods identify sequence verification and microscopy-based assessment.

edges.mechanism: The D415A construct fails to restore the motility phenotype recovered with wild-type maf. It remains an indirect cellular effect, not a direct donor-contact or transport assay.
edges.subject: d415a_variant

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Native Q2W9I6 residue 415 is D, within current PF01973 259-419 and structural 273-530. Current profile boundaries are not experimental truncations.
causal_graphs.limitations: The observed phenotype does not distinguish donor-pocket geometry, protein stability, abundance or other indirect effects. No Maf donor-binding measurement, matched variant-folding control or isolated-domain assay is shown in this experiment.
causal_graphs.scope: Single D415A substitution in full-length pAK22-maf expressed in the AMB-1 maf deletion strain; distinct from the E324A construct.
causal_graphs.title: D415A prevents Maf complementation of the tested readouts

causal_graphs.context: Maf structure 5MU5 compared with C. jejuni Cst-II; CMP-Pse5Ac7Ac is docked, not crystallographically observed in Maf. Whole-protein mutant phenotypes motivate but do not establish the proposed molecular explanation.

evidence.explanation: Figures 4/S7, docking Methods and Discussion explicitly leave catalytic identity for further testing. Sulfate overlap and a noncomplementing variant are not observation of this chemical step.

edges.mechanism: The authors propose a catalytic role for Glu324 from its position near the modeled reaction center, comparison with sialyltransferases and loss of mutant complementation. The general-base assignment is explicitly hypothetical.
edges.subject: proposed_glu324_role

evidence.explanation: HAL PDF Results page 15, adjacent structural comparison and original docking figure; the D415A cellular phenotype cannot discriminate this proposal from destabilization.
evidence.snippet: Asp415 might exercise the same role

edges.mechanism: Asp415 is proposed to organize a donor-nucleotide binding loop by analogy to Cst-II Asp154. This is a structure-based causal hypothesis, not a Maf ligand-binding measurement or demonstrated direct contact.
edges.subject: proposed_asp415_role

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Q2W9I6 E324/D415 both map within PF01973 259-419. Cst-II and its residue roles are comparison-system evidence, not direct demonstrations for this family.
causal_graphs.limitations: Precise donor stereochemistry, acceptor positioning, catalytic-base identity and donor-pocket contacts remain unresolved. No direct proton-transfer observation or mutant binding/kinetic dissection is available in the inspected study. Retain the observed phenotypes in their separate graphs.

causal_graphs.scope: Structural/docking interpretation of AMB-1 Maf Glu324 and Asp415; not experimentally resolved chemical steps or family-wide residue assignments.

record.description: This domain can be found in a group of proteins, including archaeal 6-hydroxymethylpterin diphosphokinase (6-HMDPK), known as MptE, which catalyses the formation of 6-hydroxymethyl-7,8-dihydropterin diphosphate (6-HMDP) from 6-HMD and ATP [[cite:PUB00061602]]. 6-HMDP is the precursor of the pterin containing moiety of the essential C1-carriers tetrahydrofolate and tetrahydromethanopterin. This entry also includes a number of uncharacterised proteins from bacteria.

evidence.explanation: Original Figure 4 and Methods distinguish displayed PF0930 chemistry from reported similar MJ1634 activity and E. coli complementation. The supporting purity gel concerns MJ1634.

discussions.notes: Trace the cited PF0930 expression protocol and exact constructs, reconcile 70/80 C purification wording, test natural substrate breadth and catalytic residues, and inspect later structural/biochemical work. A monophosphate workup peak is not a demonstrated enzyme step. See evidence/PF01973/crecy-2012-mpte.txt.
discussions.prompt: Resolve archaeal substrate breadth, constructs and catalytic steps beyond the reported assays.
discussions.rationale: Purified whole-protein reactions and heterologous rescue establish bounded activities, not a universal PF01973 substrate or native archaeal flux.

evidence.explanation: Figures 1/5/S1/S4 and Methods support scoped phenotypes; Figures 4/S7 are structural/docking proposals. Maf abundance/folding controls and a donor-bound Maf structure are not established by those experiments.

discussions.notes: Preserve the S283A/D318A/N491A condition-specific negative results. The N494A caption conflicts with Figure 5B, Methods, primers and sequence; use N491A for that control, not an invented variant. The paper's structural 273-530 interval differs from the current 259-419 Pfam match. Do not transfer kinase chemistry to Maf or glycosylation to archaeal MptE.
discussions.prompt: Resolve Maf donor stereochemistry and distinguish residue chemistry from protein stability or expression effects.
discussions.rationale: Deletion/rescue and E324A/D415A perturbations support cellular effects, but do not by themselves demonstrate donor transfer or acid/base catalysis by isolated PF01973.

evidence.explanation: Aeromonas Maf1 study identified for a separate full-text, construct and domain-mapping assessment; not used as evidence for the current graphs.
The 2024 multicomponent specificity study remains a full-methods/figure and exact-member follow-up; publisher access returned 403 in this session.
Clostridium mini-flagellin glycoengineering identified for further assessment; no native-substrate or direct catalytic claim is transferred from search metadata.

discussions.notes: Continue the explicit evidence/PF01973/coverage-and-exclusions.txt queue, including earlier Aeromonas, Campylobacter, Helicobacter and newer studies. Full family review remains incomplete, and all earlier corpus follow-ups stay open.
discussions.prompt: Extend PF01973 coverage through individually mapped Maf members and partner-specific experiments.
discussions.rationale: The founding archaeal and AMB-1 experiments do not exhaust later Maf specificity, glycoengineering and other bacterial contexts.
